name: Auxiliares Cornuti seniores (palatina)

abilities.name: Square
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close square formation. Note that it cannot move whilst this ability is active.

abilities.name: Spear Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

abilities.name: Barbarian Testudo
abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a static defensive formation.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

attributes.name: Formation Attack
attributes.text: The unit will try to stay in formation when in melee.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

short: Cornuti, the name of this unit from Latin can be translated as «horned», received their name apparently because of their horned helmets. According to the most popular opinion, the Cornuti unit was originally formed from Germanic men. This unit is believed to have played a prominent role during Constantine the Great's campaign in Italy in 312, as many scholars believe that the central figures of the soldiers depicted on the Arch of Constantine (the scene depicts the siege of Verona in 312) were Cornuti soldiers, due to the horn decorations on their helmets. In the middle of the 4th century, the Cornuti fought alongside the Brachiati in the Gallic army, famous for their «barritus», a special combination of martial dance and war cry. Ammianus calls them «battle-hardened» and claims that they were fearsome by their mere appearance. Recruited exclusively from Roman Gaul, they distinguished themselves in several key battles of the late period, including the Battle of Verona and at the Milvian Bridge during the civil war between Constantine and Maxentius. The Cornuti fought against the Alemanni at Argentoratum: together with the Brachiati, they formed the right flank of the Roman infantry, and were the first to meet and withstand the onslaught of the attacking Germanic cavalry.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
